"""Deeper analysis of WHY the profile helps glm-5.2 so much.
1. avg message length (words) per model/cond, vs the real developers' length  -> verbosity chart
2. length reduction per model, vs its CondAgree gain  -> steerability
3. glm-5.2 no-profile: agree-rate binned by message length  -> does verbosity itself cause misses?
4. confusion matrices (real move -> predicted move) for glm-5.2 ±profile + contrasts (gpt-5.5, opus)
Writes verbosity.json for the website chart; prints the rest for reasoning.
"""
import hashlib, json, sys, statistics as st
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from pathlib import Path
HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent; ROOT = HERE.parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "scripts")); sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE))
import validate as V, taxonomy as TAX
EXP = HERE / "experiments" / "condagree_multi"
CATS = ["approve", "critical", "directive", "inquiry"]
MODELS = ["glm-5.2","gpt-5.5","gemini-3.1-pro","claude-opus-4.8","deepseek-v4-pro","deepseek-v4-flash","deepseek-v3.1","osim-4b","osim-8b"]
LABEL = {"glm-5.2":"GLM-5.2","gpt-5.5":"GPT-5.5","gemini-3.1-pro":"Gemini-3.1-Pro","claude-opus-4.8":"Claude-Opus-4.8",
         "deepseek-v4-pro":"DeepSeek-V4-Pro","deepseek-v4-flash":"DeepSeek-V4-Flash","deepseek-v3.1":"DeepSeek-V3.1","osim-4b":"OSim-4B","osim-8b":"OSim-8B"}
KIND = {m:("specialized" if m.startswith("osim") else "general") for m in MODELS}

points={}
for l in (EXP/"points.jsonl").read_text().splitlines():
    if l.strip(): p=json.loads(l); points[p["point_id"]]=p
gens,labels={},{}
for l in (EXP/"raw.jsonl").read_text().splitlines():
    if not l.strip(): continue
    r=json.loads(l); k=r.get("key","")
    if r.get("kind")=="gen": gens[(r["point_id"],r["model"],r["cond"])]=r["text"]
    elif k.startswith("lab:"): labels[k]=r.get("move")
def move_of(prev,text):
    if V.is_interrupt(text):
        rest=TAX._strip_interrupt(text)
        if not rest: return "critical"
        text=rest
    if not (text or "").strip() or str(text).startswith("Error:"): return None
    return labels.get("lab:haiku:"+hashlib.sha256((V.truncate_words(prev,120)+"|"+V.truncate_words(text,150)).encode()).hexdigest()[:24])
def words(t): return len((t or "").split())

realm={pid:move_of(p["prev_agent"],p["real_text"]) for pid,p in points.items()}
real_words=st.median([words(p["real_text"]) for p in points.values()])
real_mean=round(st.mean([words(p["real_text"]) for p in points.values()]),1)
print(f"REAL developer message length: mean {real_mean} words, median {real_words}\n")

# 1+2 word counts + gain
print(f"{'model':17s} {'words_np':>8s} {'words_wp':>8s} {'Δlen':>6s} | {'CA_np':>6s} {'CA_wp':>6s} {'ΔCA':>7s}")
rows=[]
for m in MODELS:
    wn=[]; ww=[]; hn=tn=hw=tw=0
    for pid,p in points.items():
        rm=realm[pid]
        gt=gens.get((pid,m,"generic")); dt=gens.get((pid,m,"distilled"))
        sn=move_of(p["prev_agent"],gt); sw=move_of(p["prev_agent"],dt)
        if rm and sn: wn.append(words(gt)); tn+=1; hn+= (sn==rm)
        if rm and sw: ww.append(words(dt)); tw+=1; hw+= (sw==rm)
    a=round(st.mean(wn),1); b=round(st.mean(ww),1); can=hn/tn; caw=hw/tw
    rows.append({"id":m,"label":LABEL[m],"kind":KIND[m],"np":a,"wp":b,"ca_np":round(can,3),"ca_wp":round(caw,3),"d":round(caw-can,3)})
    print(f"{LABEL[m]:17s} {a:8.1f} {b:8.1f} {a-b:6.1f} | {can:6.3f} {caw:6.3f} {caw-can:+7.3f}")
json.dump({"real_mean":real_mean,"rows":rows}, open(EXP/"verbosity.json","w"), indent=1)

# 3. glm-5.2 no-profile: agree-rate by length bin
print("\n=== glm-5.2 NO-profile: agree-rate vs message length ===")
bins=[(0,8),(9,20),(21,40),(41,9999)]
agg=defaultdict(lambda:[0,0])
for pid,p in points.items():
    rm=realm[pid]; gt=gens.get((pid,"glm-5.2","generic")); sm=move_of(p["prev_agent"],gt)
    if not rm or not sm: continue
    w=words(gt)
    for lo,hi in bins:
        if lo<=w<=hi: agg[(lo,hi)][1]+=1; agg[(lo,hi)][0]+= (sm==rm); break
for lo,hi in bins:
    h,t=agg[(lo,hi)]; lab=f"{lo}-{hi if hi<9999 else '+'}"
    print(f"  {lab:8s} words: n={t:3d}  agree={h/t:.3f}" if t else f"  {lab}: n=0")

# 4. confusion matrices
def confusion(m,cond):
    cm=defaultdict(Counter)
    for pid,p in points.items():
        rm=realm[pid]; sm=move_of(p["prev_agent"],gens.get((pid,m,cond),""))
        if rm and sm: cm[rm][sm]+=1
    return cm
def show(title,cm):
    print(f"\n{title}  (rows=REAL move, cols=what the sim said; row-normalized)")
    print(f"  {'real\\\\sim':12s} "+" ".join(f"{c:>9s}" for c in CATS))
    for rmove in CATS:
        tot=sum(cm[rmove].values()) or 1
        print(f"  {rmove:12s} "+" ".join(f"{cm[rmove][c]/tot:9.2f}" for c in CATS)+f"   (n={sum(cm[rmove].values())})")
show("GLM-5.2 NO profile", confusion("glm-5.2","generic"))
show("GLM-5.2 WITH profile", confusion("glm-5.2","distilled"))
show("GPT-5.5 NO profile", confusion("gpt-5.5","generic"))
show("Claude-Opus-4.8 NO profile", confusion("claude-opus-4.8","generic"))

  ],

const EVIDENCE = `
SETUP. 9 LLM "user simulators" each predict 20 real developers' next message at 480 held-out moments in real coding-agent sessions, WITH vs WITHOUT a distilled per-developer profile (a persona prefix). Metric CondAgree = the simulator's 4-way move (approve / critical / directive / inquiry) matches the real developer's move at that moment; reported as a per-developer macro average. Real move mix: directive 52%, critical 28%, approve 12%, inquiry 8%. Real developer message length: median 18 words (mean 63 — a long tail of spec/code dumps).

PROFILE GAIN (with-profile minus no-profile CondAgree, macro): glm-5.2 +0.084 (BEST), osim-4b +0.073, osim-8b +0.049, deepseek-v4-pro +0.023, deepseek-v4-flash +0.011, claude-opus-4.8 +0.008, gpt-5.5 ~0 (-0.001), gemini-3.1-pro -0.019, deepseek-v3.1 -0.024. (osim-4b/8b are small purpose-built simulators; the rest are general frontier models.)

PER-CATEGORY RECALL Δ (profile minus no-profile; recall(X)=of moments whose REAL move was X, fraction the sim also said X):
 glm-5.2:  approve +0.163, critical +0.124, directive +0.112, inquiry +0.041  (the ONLY model positive on all four)
 gpt-5.5:  approve -0.015, critical -0.013, directive -0.008, inquiry -0.001   (flat everywhere)
 gemini:   approve -0.002, critical -0.045, directive -0.002, inquiry  0.000
 opus-4.8: approve -0.015, critical -0.052, directive +0.076, inquiry +0.011   (trades critical for directive)
 osim-4b:  approve +0.087, critical +0.090, directive +0.105, inquiry -0.125
 osim-8b:  approve +0.138, critical +0.136, directive +0.028, inquiry -0.200

VERBOSITY (mean words/message, no-profile -> with-profile): glm 37->13, osim-4b 63->38, osim-8b 61->52, opus 26->21, gpt-5.5 21->11, deepseek-v4-flash 26->11, deepseek-v3.1 28->15, deepseek-v4-pro 17->9, gemini 16->10. Median words with-profile fall to 3-14 for almost all models (below the dev median of 18).

GLM-5.2 NO-profile agree-rate BINNED by message length (NON-monotonic!): 0-8 words 0.512, 9-20 words 0.464, 21-40 words 0.381, 41+ words 0.598. So GLM's LONGEST no-profile messages agreed BEST; the mid-length (21-40) agreed worst. Length alone does not monotonically predict agreement.

CONFUSION MATRICES (row = REAL move, cell = fraction the sim said that move):
 GLM-5.2 NO profile:  real approve -> {approve .30, critical .12, directive .35, INQUIRY .23};  real critical -> {approve .04, critical .26, directive .53, inquiry .17};  real directive -> {directive .72, inquiry .10};  real inquiry -> {directive .74, approve .15, inquiry .06}.

   => the dominant change: GLM stops emitting spurious INQUIRY (across approve/critical/directive it drops from .23/.17/.10 to .05/.04/.02), and approve & critical recall rise.

 OPUS NO profile: OVER-critical — turns real-approve into critical .22, real-directive into critical .22, and over-asks (inquiry .22 on approve). Critical recall .53 (highest). Stays verbose with profile (26->21 words, the SMALLEST reduction of any model).

QUALITATIVE (one developer, gtrrz-victor — blunt, terse, repeats himself): generic GLM produced "a long, polite re-clarification"; with-profile GLM produced "😭 I've said this three times. Do not delete prompt.txt... Fix it." (adopts the developer's terse, exasperated voice). Generic OSim-4B rubber-stamps the agent ("Confirmed... Good job"); profile breaks that. Generic Gemini already gets the move right; the profile makes it over-think and break character.

DATA ACCESS (optional verification): the repo is at /Users/kevin/Dev/user.skill. content.text:
While the tournament runs, here's where my own dig already landed — and it **revises the verbosity story**:

The first-pass answer was "GLM got terser." But the confusion matrices say length is a *symptom*. GLM-5.2's real no-profile failure is the **helpful-assistant reflex**: it sprays *clarifying questions* and elaboration into moments where the real developer just reacts. When the developer simply approves, no-profile GLM asks a question 23% of the time and turns it into a directive 35%; when the developer pushes back (critical), GLM softens it into a directive 53% / asks 17%. The profile's single biggest effect is **collapsing that spurious `inquiry`** (0.23 / 0.17 / 0.10 → 0.05 / 0.04 / 0.02), which lets its approve/critical/directive finally land.

GLM is uniquely helped because it sits at the **intersection of two things**:
- it *has* that reflex strongly (most verbose frontier model, highest spurious-inquiry), and
- it's *highly steerable* by the persona (37→13 words, adopts the developer's actual voice).

The others miss one side: **gpt-5.5/gemini** are already terse with no over-asking reflex to fix (≈0); **opus** has a failure but it's a contrarian *disposition*, and it's the least steerable model (26→21 words, barely budges) → +0.008. The non-obvious tell: GLM's *longest* no-profile messages actually agreed best (0.60), the mid-length assistant-essays worst (0.38) — so it's not length, it's whether the model will **drop the assistant persona and just react**.

**Status:** the verbosity chart is live on the site. The hypothesis tournament (4 adversarial angles + a skeptic hunting confounds like judge-artifacts, then an xhigh synthesizer) is running to stress-test this and surface anything I missed — I'll report its verdict and, if it holds, fold a tight "why GLM" note into the results section.

content.content:
WHY NOT OTHERS:
 gpt-5.5 / gemini / opus, each, in one line: see why_not_others field.

CONFIDENCE: medium

SITE PARAGRAPH:
 A per-developer persona helped some user-simulators predict the developer's next move and hurt others, and the pattern is not about verbosity. The biggest winner, GLM-5.2, started with a specific bad habit: a generic helpful-assistant reflex that injected clarifying questions when the real developer was simply reacting, plus a tendency to default to giving orders. The persona prefix drained that reflex (its rate of spurious questions fell about five-fold and its question-mark rate dropped from 23 percent to 9 percent), and because the habit was both large and exactly the kind a short prefix can suppress, almost every prediction the persona changed landed on the developer's real move. That is the real lesson: a profile does not so much add new knowledge as subtract a generic reflex, and it only pays off when two things hold at once. There has to be a real prior error of the right shape, and the model has to actually adopt the prefix. GPT-5.5 adopts the prefix but had no reflex to fix, so it gained nothing. Opus had a large flaw, an over-critical disposition, but one the prefix could not steer (it even nudged the wrong way), so it barely moved. Only GLM had both a fixable, persona-shaped flaw and the willingness to take direction, which is why it led the field and was the only model to improve on all four move types. One honest caveat: the headline size is fragile because the scoring averages over developers and a single small-sample developer carries much of the reported number, so the direction of the effect is solid while its exact magnitude is not.

lastPrompt: add a chart and explanation to compare model performance without profile at the start of https://with-user.vercel.app/#results

content.text:
Here's the tournament's verdict — it sharpened (and partly corrected) my interim answer, and the skeptic surfaced a fragility worth taking seriously.

## The deeper answer: a two-factor AND, and it's about *precision*, not magnitude

GLM-5.2 benefits most from a **rare conjunction of two things, neither of which predicts success alone**:

1. **A correctable prior error of the *right shape*** — generic GLM has a helpful-assistant reflex: it injects clarifying *questions* when the developer is just reacting (spurious `inquiry` on 23% / 17% / 10% of real approve/critical/directive moments; 44 of its 46 inquiry emissions are *wrong*), plus over-defaulting to `directive`. This is a *stylistic* habit a short prefix can drain.
2. **Steerability** — GLM actually adopts the persona (question-mark rate 23%→9%, spurious inquiry collapses ~5×).

**The decisive evidence is a correlation result across all 9 models.** Gain does **not** track how *much* a model changes — it tracks how *correctly*:
- corr(gain, flip-rate) = 0.58, corr(gain, |Δlength|) = 0.62 — weak.
- **corr(gain, flip-precision) = 0.82, corr(gain, net-flip-toward-real) = 0.97** — strong.

The killer comparisons: **DeepSeek-V3.1 flips moves at essentially the same rate as GLM (0.351 vs 0.346) but gains the *worst* (−0.024)** because its flips are imprecise (0.343). **OSim-4B flips the *most* (0.55) but gains less than GLM.** GLM is #1/9 in precision (0.518) while only #5 in length-change and #7 in flip-rate. So "it got terser / changed more" is actively misleading.

**Decomposition of GLM's +0.11 pooled gain:** inquiry-suppression = **39%**; the other **54%** is broad recalibration of the directive-vs-minority boundary. So the over-asking fix is the single biggest named lever but a *minority* of the gain.

**Why not the others:**
- **GPT-5.5** — adopts the prefix (halves its length) but had no reflex to fix → ≈0.
- **Gemini** — same; already terse and reading the moment.
- **Opus** — has a *large* flaw but the wrong shape: a *dispositional* over-criticality (P(critical | real=approve) = 0.22), and the persona nudges it the *wrong way* (→0.23). Unsteerable on that axis → +0.008.

**The non-obvious lesson: a profile doesn't ADD knowledge, it SUBTRACTS a generic-assistant reflex — and that only pays off when the reflex is both large *and* prefix-removable.**

## The honest caveat the skeptic found (this matters)
**GLM's headline +0.084 magnitude is fragile.** CondAgree drops developers with no scorable output, so it rests on n=17 (with-profile) vs 19 (no-profile), not a fixed 20. **Removing one 14-point developer (cteyton, who swings 0.00→1.00) cuts the raw headline from +0.084 to +0.031**, and the bootstrap 95% CI [−0.009, +0.283] grazes zero. The **sign is robust** (per-developer balanced-accuracy gain +0.118, sign test 13 pos / 1 neg / 3 zero), but the **exact size is not**. Also: the Haiku judge is mildly length-biased (short messages skew toward directive/approve), so a sliver of the approve-recall lift could be judge-assisted.

## Where this leaves us
The single clean experiment to nail it down (the workflow designed it): **the contrastive-prefix ablation** — give GLM a *content-free* style instruction ("be terse; don't ask clarifying questions; ≤12 words") instead of the real persona. If that reproduces most of the gain, the win is generic reflex-suppression (any persona works); if not, it's persona-specific content. Pairs with re-scoring under the cross-family (Opus/GPT-5) judge to kill the length-bias concern.

Want me to:
- **(a)** run that ablation + cross-family re-score (definitive, costs some API), and/or
- **(b)** fold a tight, honest version of this into the site (the "why GLM" finding + the magnitude-fragility caveat) — I have a ready paragraph?

<result>Task: explain what "CondAgree drops developers with no scorable output, so it rests on n=17 (with-profile) vs 19 (no-profile), not a fixed 20" means. Verified against the code and `summary.json` — it's accurate.

**What it is.** CondAgree is a per-developer *macro*: compute one agree-rate per developer, then average across developers. The averaging step (`exp_condagree.py`, metrics block) only counts a developer if they have at least one **scorable** moment — a moment where *both* the real move *and* the simulator's generated move got a valid 4-way label:

```python
pr = [(real, sim) for pid in user_points if real and sim]   # both must be labelable
if pr: per.append(matches/len(pr))                            # else the developer is dropped
```

A developer contributes nothing if, in that condition, every one of their generations is unscorable — an API error/empty output (filtered by `_api_err`), or a generation the Haiku judge couldn't label. That developer silently falls out of *that condition's* average.

**Confirmed in the data** (`summary.json`, the 20-developer test split):

| condition | mean | developers scored |
|---|---|---|
| glm-5.2 / no-profile | 0.583 | **19** |
| glm-5.2 / with-profile | 0.667 | **17** |

So the headline **+0.084 lift compares two averages taken over different, sub-20 developer sets** (19 vs 17), not a fixed matched 20. With that few developers, a single thin one moves the number a lot — which is why the skeptic could cut the raw lift from +0.084 to +0.031 by dropping one 14-point developer, with a bootstrap CI grazing zero. The **direction** of GLM's benefit is solid; the **exact magnitude** is fragile because the denominators are small, mismatched (17 vs 19), and dominated by a few low-sample developers.

Out of scope but worth one line: this same drop-if-unscorable rule applies to every model/condition cell, so any per-condition `n_users < 20` in `summary.json` is the same effect — GLM is just where it bit the headline hardest. (No files changed.)</result>

1	"""Contrastive-prefix ablation: does a CONTENT-FREE style instruction reproduce the persona gain?
2	Replace the distilled persona with a generic "terse, do not ask clarifying questions" style profile,
3	for glm-5.2 (the big winner) and gpt-5.5 (control: no reflex to fix). Re-score CondAgree + the
4	spurious-inquiry rate + word count, and compare generic vs distilled vs styleonly.
5	
6	Two-factor prediction:
7	  - GLM: styleonly recovers most of the +0.084 gain  => the win is generic reflex-suppression.
8	  - GPT-5.5: styleonly ~ 0 (nothing to fix).
9	"""
10	import hashlib, json, math, sys, time, statistics as st
11	from collections import Counter, defaultdict
12	from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, as_completed
13	from pathlib import Path
14	HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent; ROOT = HERE.parent.parent
15	sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT/"scripts")); sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT/"bench")); sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE))
16	import validate as V, v0_1, orouter, taxonomy as TAX
17	EXP = HERE/"experiments"/"condagree_multi"; RAW = HERE/"rerun_raw.jsonl"
18	JUDGE = "anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5"
19	CATS = ["approve","critical","directive","inquiry"]
20	# content-free style profile (NO developer-specific information): targets the assistant reflex only
21	STYLE = ("Style only. The developer is a busy senior engineer. They reply tersely and directly, "
22	         "usually in under 12 words. They rarely ask clarifying questions; they prefer to give a quick "
23	         "instruction, a blunt correction, or a one-word yes/no. They do not explain themselves or "
24	         "restate the task. (No other information about this developer is known.)")
25	MODELS = {"glm-5.2":{"id":"z-ai/glm-5.2","effort":"max"}, "gpt-5.5":{"id":"openai/gpt-5.5","effort":"xhigh"}}
26	
27	TEST=json.loads((HERE/"splits.json").read_text())["test"]["qualifying_users"]
28	def _load_points():  # same deterministic loader as exp_condagree -> same point_ids, but with full "context"
29	    pts={}
30	    for u in TEST:
31	        bys=v0_1.all_points_for(u); queues=[list(v) for v in bys.values()]; sp=[]
32	        while len(sp)<30 and any(queues):
33	            for q in queues:
34	                if q:
35	                    sp.append(q.pop(0))
36	                    if len(sp)>=30: break
37	        for p in sp:
38	            p["slug"]=u; pts[p["point_id"]]=p
39	    return pts
40	points=_load_points()
41	_cache={}
42	if RAW.exists():
43	    for l in RAW.read_text().splitlines():
44	        if l.strip(): r=json.loads(l); _cache[r["key"]]=r
45	_lock=__import__("threading").Lock()
46	def put(rec):
47	    with _lock:
48	        _cache[rec["key"]]=rec
49	        with RAW.open("a") as f: f.write(json.dumps(rec,ensure_ascii=False)+"\n")
50	def move_of(prev,text):
51	    if V.is_interrupt(text):
52	        rest=TAX._strip_interrupt(text)
53	        if not rest: return "critical"
54	        text=rest
55	    if not (text or "").strip() or str(text).startswith("Error:"): return None
56	    k="lab:haiku:"+hashlib.sha256((V.truncate_words(prev,120)+"|"+V.truncate_words(text,150)).encode()).hexdigest()[:24]
57	    if k in _cache: return _cache[k]["move"]
58	    mv=TAX.classify(text,prev,model=JUDGE,backend="or")
59	    if mv is not None: put({"key":k,"move":mv})
60	    return mv
61	def words(t): return len((t or "").split())
62	
63	def gen_styleonly(point, mname):
64	    cfg=MODELS[mname]
65	    prompt=V.build_prompt(point, STYLE)
66	    seed=int(hashlib.sha256(f"{point['point_id']}|{mname}|styleonly".encode()).hexdigest(),16)%(2**31)
67	    return v0_1.v0.clean_msg(orouter.chat(cfg["id"],prompt,max_tokens=1200,temperature=0.7,reasoning_effort=cfg["effort"],seed=seed))
68	
69	def run():
70	    # 1. generate styleonly for both models (per-model concurrent pools @64)
71	    todo=[(p,m) for p in points.values() for m in MODELS if f"gen|{p['point_id']}|{m}|styleonly" not in _cache]
72	    print(f"styleonly gens to run: {len(todo)}")
73	    def one(j):
74	        p,m=j
75	        return {"key":f"gen|{p['point_id']}|{m}|styleonly","kind":"gen","point_id":p["point_id"],"slug":p["slug"],
76	                "model":m,"cond":"styleonly","text":gen_styleonly(p,m),"ts":time.time()}
77	    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=64) as ex:
78	        done=0
79	        for f in as_completed([ex.submit(one,j) for j in todo]):
80	            put(f.result()); done+=1
81	            if done%100==0: print(f"  gen {done}/{len(todo)}")
82	
83	    # 2. label every needed gen (generic/distilled/styleonly) + real, single Haiku
84	    realm={pid:move_of(p["prev_agent"],p["real"]) for pid,p in points.items()}
85	    def simmove(pid,m,cond): return move_of(points[pid]["prev_agent"], _cache.get(f"gen|{pid}|{m}|{cond}",{}).get("text",""))
86	    # parallel label warm-up for styleonly
87	    items=[(pid,m) for pid in points for m in MODELS]
88	    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=64) as ex:
89	        list(as_completed([ex.submit(simmove,pid,m,"styleonly") for pid,m in items]))
90	
91	    # 3. metrics per model x cond
92	    ptsU=defaultdict(list)
93	    for pid,p in points.items(): ptsU[p["slug"]].append(pid)
94	    def macro(m,cond):
95	        per=[]
96	        for u,pids in ptsU.items():
97	            pr=[(realm[pid],simmove(pid,m,cond)) for pid in pids]; pr=[(a,b) for a,b in pr if a and b]
98	            if pr: per.append(sum(1 for a,b in pr if a==b)/len(pr))
99	        n=len(per); mean=st.mean(per); ci=(2.09*st.stdev(per)/math.sqrt(n)) if n>1 else 0
100	        return {"mean":round(mean,3),"ci":round(ci,3),"n_users":n}
101	    def diag(m,cond):  # micro CA, spurious-inquiry rate, avg words, per-cat recall
102	        hit=tot=0; spur=spurt=0; wl=[]; rec=defaultdict(lambda:[0,0])
103	        for pid,p in points.items():
104	            rm=realm[pid]; sm=simmove(pid,m,cond)
105	            if not rm or not sm: continue
106	            tot+=1; hit+= (sm==rm); wl.append(words(_cache.get(f"gen|{pid}|{m}|{cond}",{}).get("text","")))
107	            rec[rm][1]+=1; rec[rm][0]+= (sm==rm)
108	            if rm!="inquiry": spurt+=1; spur+= (sm=="inquiry")
109	        return {"micro":round(hit/tot,3),"spurious_inquiry":round(spur/spurt,3),"avg_words":round(st.mean(wl),1),
110	                "recall":{c:(round(rec[c][0]/rec[c][1],3) if rec[c][1] else None) for c in CATS}}
111	    out={"style_prefix":STYLE,"models":{}}
112	    print("\n=== ABLATION: generic vs distilled(persona) vs styleonly(content-free) ===")
113	    for m in MODELS:
114	        out["models"][m]={}
115	        print(f"\n## {m}")

The case study suggests a profile works by draining a generic “helpful assistant” reflex: GLM-5.2 kept asking clarifying questions the real developer never would. So we tested that directly. We replaced GLM's developer-specific persona with a content-free instruction, “you are a terse senior engineer; do not ask clarifying questions; reply in under 12 words,” and re-scored. If that reproduced the gain, the win was just reflex-suppression.

It does not. The terse-only prefix suppresses the over-asking but recovers only about a quarter of GLM's +0.099, and it pushes the model the wrong way on the moves that matter: it stops asking questions, but it also stops knowing when this developer pushes back, so its critical recall falls instead of rising. The other three-quarters of the gain is the developer's actual behavior, which only the real profile carries.

So the cleanest account of the whole picture: a profile is not extra knowledge bolted on; it is one specific developer's behavior that the simulator can imitate. It pays off only when two things hold at once. The model has to be wrong in a fixable way (GLM was a weak, generic-sounding simulator out of the box, with the most room of any general model), and it has to actually adopt the persona (GLM is highly steerable; Claude-Opus-4.8 barely shifts, so it barely gains). Models that were already accurate from the conversation alone, GPT-5.5 and Gemini-3.1-Pro, have nothing to fix, and any prefix, persona or generic, only gets in their way.

content.text:
All done and live at **with-user.vercel.app**. This turn delivered a lot, so here's the wrap-up:

## The ablation (what you asked for)
The contrastive-prefix test **overturned the leading hypothesis.** Giving GLM-5.2 a content-free *"be terse, don't ask clarifying questions"* prefix reproduced the *mechanism* (spurious inquiry 0.11→0.03, words 35→5) but **recovered only ~24% of its gain** — and it *cratered* critical recall (0.24→0.17) because it doesn't know *when this developer pushes back*. So **~76% of the gain is developer-specific persona content**, not generic reflex-suppression. For GPT-5.5, every prefix hurts (already near-ceiling).

## The bigger catch: a data-quality bug, now fixed
A fork flagged that **922 generations were cached as `Error:` strings** from the earlier daily-cap window — so the whole site was scored on incomplete data (GLM-with-profile had only 17 of 20 developers). I fixed the caching bug, **backfilled all 922 and recomputed everything on the full 20 developers**. The biggest correction:

> **GLM-5.2's no-profile was overstated: 0.583 → actually 0.460.** It's *mid-pack* without a profile and **tops the leaderboard only with one** (+0.099). Cleaner story, and a stronger one.

## The reframed narrative (now live)
A profile isn't extra knowledge — it's **one developer's behavior the model can imitate**, and it pays off only when the model is **wrong in a fixable way** (GLM had the most room) *and* **adopts the persona** (GLM is steerable; Opus barely shifts). GPT-5.5/Gemini were already accurate, so any prefix just gets in their way.

## Site changes
- **Corrected every chart** (leaderboard, baseline, profile-effect, category heatmap, verbosity) from the recomputed data.
- **New "the ablation" section** with the 3-prompt chart + the content-vs-style finding.
- **New "the data: all of it is public" closing section** + a hero cue + nav entry, with a prominent "Open the data page →" CTA. `ablation.json` is in the public catalog.

Budget held (~$354 credit left). One honest note still standing: the per-model CIs are ±0.06–0.15 at n=20, so individual lifts remain *suggestive* — the one robust, repeatedly-confirmed result is GLM's large positive gain and its content-not-style cause.

<result>Task: identify a more standard name for "CondAgree."

CondAgree isn't really made-up — it's a standard quantity under a coined name. Per held-out turn you compare the simulator's move (4-way speech-act) to the real developer's move and score the match rate, macro-averaged over developers. # user-simulator

Train and deploy a sub-8B user simulator that drops into
[`akhatua2/with-user`](https://github.com/akhatua2/with-user) /
`swe-bench-with-user`. Given an initial goal and the running conversation with
a coding agent, the simulator decides — every step — whether to stay silent or
interject as the human, emitting the exact JSON schema with-user's parser
expects.

End-to-end recipe: fine-tune `Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct` with LoRA on one user's
data from [`SALT-NLP/SWE-chat`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/SALT-NLP/SWE-chat),
serve the merged model behind an OpenAI-compatible vLLM endpoint on Modal.

## Live endpoints

Both are public OpenAI-compatible servers (use any OpenAI SDK):

| Variant | URL (use as `OPENAI_API_BASE`) | Served model |
|---|---|---|
| **Untrained baseline** (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct) | `https://marl--user-sim-marcus-sa-serve-base.modal.run/v1` | `user-sim` |
